## GOV-003 source map — AMLO / Mexico / 2022 / Chapter 5B

**Source role and scope.** Executive official press communiqué from Mexico’s Ministry of Finance (SHCP), dated 30 January 2023, reporting fourth-quarter/full-year 2022 economic conditions, public finances, and public debt. It is an issuer-authored summary, not the underlying statistical report or an audit. Its stated institutional role is official dissemination; the page says each agency/entity is strictly responsible for the legality, veracity, and quality of information it provides. **Locators:** blocks 1, 7.

**Accounting/measurement limitations.** The extract does not state whether fiscal figures use cash or accrual accounting, whether coverage is central government or consolidated public sector except where labels specify “Government Federal” or “public sector,” whether figures are audited/provisional, or the deflator/base for “real” growth. It mixes pesos, US dollars, GDP shares, real annual changes, and budget-program comparisons. The webpage links to more detailed statistics but they are not included. **Locators:** blocks 4–7.

### Atomic claims

| ID | Claim | Character | Locator |
|---|---|---|---|
| GOV-003-01 | SHCP states that, at the end of the administration’s fourth year, public finances had responsible resource management, stable debt, and efficient welfare-oriented spending. | Official assertion; evaluative, not independently demonstrated here. | block 1 |
| GOV-003-02 | Public debt was **49.4% of GDP** in 2022, stated as **1.6 percentage points of GDP below budgeted** and **1.4 points below 2021**. | Official reported outcome; debt definition/coverage not supplied in extract. | block 1 |
| GOV-003-03 | SHCP attributes the debt result to budgetary income performance, stating that income remained **1.5% of GDP above budget** even after the fuel IEPS subsidy. | Official causal attribution; requires budget-execution verification. | block 1 |
| GOV-003-04 | The communiqué reports Mexican economic growth of **2.9% accumulated through November 2022**, describing it as better than analysts expected and supported by labour-market performance, consumption, and private investment. | Reported figure plus official interpretation/attribution; it is not a full-year growth figure in this extract. | block 2 |
| GOV-003-05 | It reports unemployment of **2.8% overall** and **2.5% for women** at end-2022, and **2.4 million jobs** created in 2022, “mostly formal.” | Official reported indicators; the extract does not define the employment series or causal basis. | block 2 |
| GOV-003-06 | Private consumption grew **7.1% through October 2022**, versus a stated historical average of **2.7%**; services consumption had recovered pre-pandemic levels. | Official reported comparison; comparison period/methodology for the historical average are unstated. | block 2 |
| GOV-003-07 | Gross fixed investment grew **5.5% annually through October**, compared with **1.6%** historical average for the same period; machinery/equipment rose **12.2%**, compared with **5.0%** historical average. | Official reported comparison; not a fiscal-outturn measure. | block 3 |
| GOV-003-08 | Public revenues in 2022 totalled **MXN 6.595 trillion**, **MXN 422 billion above programme**, and were **2.5% higher than 2021**; the extract does not explicitly label this last change nominal or real. | Official reported fiscal outturn; budget baseline and sector coverage need verification. | block 4 |
| GOV-003-09 | Federal Government income was **MXN 632 billion above programme**; SHCP says **MXN 397 billion** of this corresponded to lower revenue from the fuel IEPS stimulus. | Official accounting statement; wording is potentially ambiguous and should be reopened against full tables. | block 4 |
| GOV-003-10 | Petroleum revenues were **MXN 1.482 trillion (5.2% of GDP)**, up **18.7% in real annual terms** from 2021; SHCP links this to high oil prices. | Official reported result and attribution; commodity-price dependence is material. | block 4 |
| GOV-003-11 | SHCP states tax-evasion enforcement improved tax income without creating or increasing taxes; non-fuel-IEPS tax revenue was **13.6% of GDP** and up **7.8% real annually**. | Official assertion plus figures; enforcement effect is not isolated in extract. | block 4 |
| GOV-003-12 | Public-sector spending was **MXN 7.569 trillion (26.5% of GDP)**, up **4.1% real annually**. Social-protection spending rose **8.7% real** to **5.3% of GDP**; physical investment rose **25.2%** to **3.3% of GDP**. | Official reported outturns; execution quality, project composition, and distributional incidence absent. | block 5 |
| GOV-003-13 | Fiscal aggregates were a **0.5% of GDP primary deficit**, **3.4% public deficit**, and **4.4% Public Sector Borrowing Requirements (RFSP)**. | Official reported aggregates; definitions and reconciliation are absent. | block 5 |
| GOV-003-14 | SHCP says fiscal buffers totalled **US$262 billion**, comprising international reserves, the IMF Flexible Credit Line, the Federal Reserve swap line, and stabilization funds. | Official assertion/reporting; availability, drawability, and component values are not supplied. | block 5 |
| GOV-003-15 | Debt operations included October buybacks of **MXN 68.017bn** maturing 2023–46 alongside **MXN 48.596bn** long-term bond/Udibono sales; later Bondes G and Bono M issues/buybacks are specified. | Official transaction report. | block 6 |
| GOV-003-16 | SHCP says buyback operations reduced average debt pressures for 2023 and the following two years by **73%**, freeing **US$3bn** for the next administration. | Official result/interpretation; baseline, calculation, and whether “pressures” means maturities or financing needs require reopening. | block 6 |
| GOV-003-17 | The government reports 21 international recognitions over four years and investment grade/stable outlook from eight rating agencies. | Official assertion; agencies, dates, and rating actions are not named. | block 6 |

**Contrary material / unresolved issues.** The extract itself identifies high oil prices as a revenue driver, weakening any inference that revenue/debt changes were solely policy-caused. It also reports deficits and RFSP rather than a surplus. No allegations, audit findings, arrears, contingent liabilities, off-budget obligations, debt currency/maturity composition, interest burden, revisions, or adverse rating evidence appear in the supplied text. **Locators:** blocks 4–6.

**Reopen with stronger evidence.** Retrieve the linked detailed finance/debt statistics and full quarterly report to verify accounting basis, audit/provisional status, budget baseline, debt universe, RFSP reconciliation, IEPS wording, buffer composition, and the 73% calculation. Cross-check macro series with INEGI/Banxico and fiscal/debt claims with official execution and debt-management publications; independently verify ratings and awards.
